UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

FORM 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025

PART IItem 1.Business
PART IItem 1A.Risk Factors
PART IIItem 7.Management's Discussion and Analysis

PART I

Item 1

ITEM 1. BUSINESS

Management believes we are a technology company whose mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We develop and support software, services, devices, and solutions.

Our cloud business provides a platform for customers, and cloud demand continued to exceed our available capacity during the year. We continue to invest in artificial intelligence capabilities. Competition in the technology sector is intense.

Capital expenditure and additions to property and equipment support our datacenter footprint. Management reviews datacenter capacity regularly. We are expanding datacenter capacity significantly, and our datacenter build-out is constrained by power and energy availability in certain regions. Construction of new datacenters continued throughout the year.

PART I

Item 1A

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties.

We face intense competition across all markets for our products and services, which may adversely affect our results of operations.

Management believes our competitors range in size from diversified global companies to small specialized firms. Competition among platform-based ecosystems remains intense and competitors may offer lower prices in every market we serve.

Our focus on cloud-based and AI services presents execution and competitive risks.

We are devoting significant resources to develop and deploy cloud-based and artificial intelligence services. Our competitors are also investing heavily in these areas.

Cyberattacks and security vulnerabilities could lead to reduced revenue, increased costs, and liability claims.

Threat actors, including nation-state actors, continue to target our products, services, devices, and customer data. A cybersecurity incident could result in remediation costs.

We may experience supply or quality problems.

Our devices and datacenter operations depend on components and materials that may be subject to shortages, tariffs, or extended lead times from a limited number of suppliers.

Our business depends on our ability to attract and retain talented employees.

Competition for highly skilled employees remains strong. Changes in headcount, workforce reductions, or severance actions could affect operating expenses.

Constraints on datacenter capacity, power, and energy availability may limit our ability to meet demand.

Our ability to grow cloud revenue depends on adding datacenter capacity. Construction delays, equipment lead times, and constraints on power and energy availability could limit capacity.

Environmental, social, and governance expectations expose us to increased compliance and reputational risk.

We are subject to evolving sustainability regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations.

Item 1B

ITEM 1B. UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS

None.

PART II

Item 7

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Fiscal Year 2025 Compared with Fiscal Year 2024. Revenue increased driven by growth in our cloud services and continued cloud demand. Management identified factors affecting gross margin; gross margin percentage decreased driven by scaling our AI infrastructure and higher depreciation from datacenter assets.

Management noted that cost of revenue increased driven by growth in cloud services, datacenter costs, and depreciation. Operating expenses increased driven by investments in cloud engineering and artificial intelligence. Useful lives of server assets were reviewed during the period.

Capital expenditures, including additions to property and equipment and finance leases, increased significantly, driven by investments to support cloud demand and our artificial intelligence infrastructure. Datacenter capacity constraints and power availability affected the pace of the build. We expect capital expenditures to increase.

Management reported that cash flow from operations increased driven by higher cash receipts from customers, partially offset by higher capital expenditure. We returned cash to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the period.
